findings.body:
### 🔵 Needs a closer look JMS cross-thread completion remains untested, and the callback lifecycle changes warrant human review.
1 open issue - [Add cross-thread JMS callback tests for context propagation and telemetry](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20678#discussion_r4308246261) · New
Review effort: Balanced

[Testing] Both new `JmsAsyncProducerTest` suites invoke completion callbacks on the sending thread. Changing a context value to `"callback-thread"` does not test the thread handoff introduced here. Add installed-agent tests for javax and jakarta JMS that invoke success and failure callbacks on a worker thread, with deterministic synchronization. Verify that the callback sees the captured caller context, restores the worker's previous context, leaves the sender's context intact, and records exactly one send span and metric observation. Include a callback overlapping the send to cover completion while the sender's scope is still open.

Record missing `error.type` on failed Camel and Lambda SQS message operations, and defer JMS asynchronous send completion until the terminal callback. Apply classification to spans and existing matching metrics without marking recovered exchanges or successful partial-batch invocations failed.

- **Camel:** Classify exception-free terminal faults as `_OTHER`, including metrics emitted when route spans are suppressed; retain exception classification.
- **Lambda SQS:** Preserve false per-message outcomes through completion, setting `ERROR` and `_OTHER` without affecting successful messages or the enclosing invocation.
- **JMS:** Finish sends exactly once on callback or synchronous throw. Restore the caller’s context around callbacks so subsequent sends remain instrumented; preserve callback exceptions and JMS 1.1 compatibility.
metadata.title: Fix messaging error classification and JMS asynchronous send completion
